questions.q: The atomic nucleus was discovered by
questions.explanation: The atomic nucleus was discovered by Rutherford, through his famous alpha- particle gold foil experiment. Info Bits: He wanted to find out the arrangement of electrons within an atom, so he designed an experiment in which fast- moving alpha particles (doubly charged helium atoms) were made to fall on a thin gold foil. He expected that alpha particles would be deflected by the subatomic particles in the gold atoms. But large deflections were not expected as alpha particles were much heavier than the protons. Most of the alpha particles passed straight from the gold foil, which means most of the space in the atom is empty. Some of them were deflected by small angles indicating that the positive charge of the atom occupies very little space and surprisingly one out of every 12,000 particles appeared to rebound (deflected by 180 degrees) indicating the concentration of all the positive charge and mass of the gold foil atom in a very small volume within the atom called the Nucleus. Thus, the atomic nucleus was discovered and he also calculated that the radius of the nucleus is about 105105 times less than the radius of the atom

questions.q: The antifreeze used in automobiles chiefly contains
questions.explanation: The antifreeze used in automobiles chiefly contains Ethylene Glycol. It is a non- volatile compound, when added to water it decreases the freezing point of the water by reducing the vapour pressure of the solution (water + ethylene glycol) and increases its boiling point hence acting as a coolant as well. Info Bits: Vapour pressure: It can be defined as the measure of the tendency of a substance to change into a gaseous (Vapor) state. It is a pressure exerted by a vapour in thermodynamic equilibrium with its condensed phase (either solid or liquid). Non- volatile compound: These are the substances when added to a solvent decreases its freezing point and increases its boiling point. Their tendency is not to vaporize easily. The freezing point of a substance can be defined as the temperature at which the vapour pressure of the substance in its liquid phase is equal to its vapour pressure in the solid phase. A solution will freeze when its vapour pressure becomes equal to the vapour pressure of the pure solid solvent. The addition of a non- volatile solid into the solvent decreases its vapour pressure i.e., it would now become equal to that of the solid solvent at a lower temperature. Thus the freezing point of the solvent decreases. Info Bits: As we know that water is a liquid and when it will freeze it will change into a solid state. The particles or atoms of a liquid are less organized when compared to a solid, so to get converted into a solid (when water will freeze) the liquid atom will have to attain a compact crystalline structure (i.e., atoms will have to lose kinetic energy to get more organized). If we add any non- volatile substance to a liquid then it will not be possible for the liquid to get organized at the same temperature at which it used to get organized or frozen earlier because the atoms of the non- volatile substance are also present. It will be required to reduce the temperature even further to get them frozen. This same thing happens when we add ethylene glycol to water, and hence its freezing point decreases. (i.e., the liquid will freeze at a temperature lower than its actual freezing point for example if it was freezing at 0∘C0∘C earlier, now it would freeze at −2∘−2∘ or −4∘C−4∘C). Also, we know that Boiling is a bulk phenomenon. When water boils the water molecules at the surface change into vapor form from the earlier liquid form. And after the addition of any non- volatile substance, the particles of that substance will also be present at the surface. So the amount of water molecules getting converted into vapour form will be less than the earlier value (i.e., vapour pressure would reduce). So more energy or temperature would be required to boil water or get it converted into vapour form. Hence, the boiling point increases with the addition of a non- volatile substance

Hydrogen atoms present in the water molecule are bonded to the oxygen atom by covalent bonds. A covalent bond is a type of bond in which atoms share electrons between them. In the case of water molecules, the electrons are not equally shared between the hydrogen and oxygen atom. The electrons are more attracted towards the oxygen as the nucleus of the oxygen atom has more protons (8) in comparison to the nucleus of Hydrogen which contains only 1 proton. The larger affinity of covalent bonded electrons towards oxygen is due to the positive charge of protons. This makes the Oxygen atom of the water molecule slightly negative (negative polarity) and the hydrogen atom slightly positive (positive polarity). This also explains the Dipolar nature of the Water molecules and helps it in attracting and dissolving ionic or polar molecules. Due to this polarity or difference of charge, one water molecule attracts another water molecule through a force of attraction called a ‘Hydrogen Bond’. The hydrogen atom of a water molecule is attracted to the oxygen atom of the adjacent water molecule, thus forming a hydrogen bond between them. This property helps water to surround the solute with water molecules from all directions. Due to hydrogen bonding with polar molecules, covalent compounds like alcohol and carbohydrates dissolves in water. Hydrogen Bond is a weak bond when compared to an Ionic or Covalent bond because in this bond actual transfer or sharing of electrons does not take place. Example: when we dissolve NaCl (sodium chloride, also known as table salt) in water. It will dissociate and sodium ions having the positive charge will get attracted to the oxygen atom having the negative polarity and chlorine ions having the negative charge will be attracted towards the positive polarity of the Hydrogen. questions.explanation: The density of water is highest at the temperature of 4∘C4∘C Info Bits: Thermal expansion of water: It has been observed that Water contracts on heating between 0∘C0∘C and 4∘C4∘C temperature. The volume of a given amount of water decreases as it is cooled from room temperature (i.e., when the temperature is decreased from room temperature) until it reaches 4∘C4∘C. Below 4∘C4∘C the volume increases, and therefore the density decreases (as we know that the Density of a body is mass per unit volume [d=m/v][d=m/v] , thus the density of a body is inversely proportional to the volume of that body. If the volume of the body increases, the density would decrease and vice versa). This property of water is also known as anomalous expansion of water. Hence, we can say that water has a maximum density at 4∘C4∘C. This property of the water helps in preserving aquatic life during winter. Water bodies like lakes and ponds start freezing during winter, and they freeze at the top first. As the temperature drops down towards 4∘C4∘C , water near the surface loses energy to the atmosphere, becomes denser (as explained above) and moves towards the lower layer of the water body and the warmer and less dense water at the bottom layer rises towards the top layer of the water body. When the colder water on top of the water body reaches a temperature below 4∘C4∘C , water becomes less dense and remains at the surface, where it freezes. In the absence of this property of water, the water bodies would have frozen from bottom to top and aquatic life would have been destroyed during the winters

Eg. burning of coal, formation of water from hydrogen and oxygen atom, etc Decomposition Reaction: These are opposite to combination reactions. Exothermic Reaction: Reaction in which energy is given out with the formation of a product is called exothermic reaction. Eg- reaction of calcium oxide (slaked- lime) with water, Burning of Natural Gas, respiration, Decomposition of vegetable matter into compost, etc. Displacement Reaction: When an element displaces another element from its compound, the reaction involved is called displacement reaction. Eg- A displacement reaction takes place when copper metal is added to a solution of silver nitrate (AgNO3). Because copper is more reactive than silver, it displaces silver out of the solution, forming silver metal and copper(II) nitrate (Cu(NO3)2). The solution's blue color denotes the presence of copper (II) ions. Double- Displacement Reaction: When two or more atoms or ions get displaced, the reaction involved is called Double- Displacement Reaction. Oxidation is the gain of an oxygen atom or loss of a hydrogen atom. Reduction is the loss of an oxygen atom or gain of a hydrogen atom

questions.explanation: Smog is an example of Air Pollution. The word 'Smog is derived from the two words Smoke and Fog. Smog has two types; one is classical smog and another is photochemical smog. Burning coal, petrol, diesel, and other fossil fuels releases harmful gases like: Carbon dioxide CO2CO2 Carbon monoxide COCO Sulfur dioxide SO2SO2 Nitrogen oxides NOxNOx Particulate matter These gases are the primary contributors to air pollution and global warming. Thus, burning fossil fuels is the major cause of air pollution. Info Bits: Classical Smog: This type of smog occurs in cool humid climates. It is a mixture of smoke, fog and sulfur dioxide. It is a reducing mixture so chemically it is also known as reducing smog. Photochemical Smog: This type of smog is common in warm, dry and sunny climates. The main components (ozone, nitric oxide, acrolein, formaldehyde and Peroxyacetyl nitrate (PAN)) of the photochemical smog result from the action of sunlight on unsaturated hydrocarbons and Nitrogen oxides produced by automobiles and factories. Photochemical smog consists of a high concentration of oxidizing agents and is, therefore, called oxidizing smog. Formation of Photochemical smog: When fossil fuels are burnt, a variety of pollutants are emitted into the troposphere. Two of these emitted pollutants are Hydrocarbons (Unburnt fuel) and nitric oxide (NO). When their emission reaches a certain higher level, a chain reaction occurs as they interact with the sunlight in which NO is converted into NO2NO2 (nitrogen dioxide). This NO2NO2 absorbs energy from sunlight and breaks up into nitric oxide and free oxygen atoms. NO2(g)→NO(g)+O(g)(1)NO2(g)→NO(g)+O(g)(1) Oxygen atoms are very reactive and combine with the O2O2 in the air to produce ozone. O(g)+O2(g)→O3(g)(2)O(g)+O2(g)→O3(g)(2) The ozone thus formed reacts rapidly with the NONO (formed in reaction 1) to regenerate NO2NO2. NO2NO2 is a brown- colored gas and when it reaches a sufficiently high level, it contributes to Haze
